findings.description: The new file count includes tracked files that have been deleted from the working tree. `git ls-files` lists index entries regardless of whether their files exist, so removing tracked System Zone files no longer produces the integrity mismatch that the previous filesystem count detected.
findings.failure_mode: An incomplete installation with missing tracked scripts or skills passes this preflight integrity check because ACTUAL_COUNT still matches the manifest count.
findings.suggested_fix: Count tracked paths that actually exist in the manifest-owning working tree, or explicitly detect deleted tracked paths with `git ls-files --deleted` and report an integrity mismatch.

findings.cross_file_justification: The PR modifies at least 15 files under .claude/ (model-config.yaml, check-loa.sh, preflight.sh, generated-model-maps.sh, CLAUDE.loa.md, 8 bridgebuilder-review dist/resources files) but .claude/checksums.json is absent from the complete 72-file change list (22 shown + 50 truncated). check_integrity hashes every manifest path and emits 'Tampered' on mismatch.
findings.description: The per-file sidecar .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml.checksum was regenerated, but the System Zone manifest .claude/checksums.json that check_integrity (and preflight.sh's count check) read was not. If the manifest is committed per-PR rather than regenerated at release, every downstream mount running check-loa.sh after this merge reports 'Tampered: .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh', 'Tampered: .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml', etc., and the integrity gate fails.
findings.failure_mode: check-loa.sh integrity check fails with multiple 'Tampered' lines on a clean checkout; preflight file-count check may also warn if the bridgebuilder dist set changed count.
findings.suggested_fix: Run tools/gen-checksums.sh and commit the regenerated .claude/checksums.json in this PR, or state in the PR that the manifest is regenerated by the release pipeline and add that to the bats test expectations.

findings.description: check_integrity now ends with an unconditional 'return 0'. Previously the function's exit status was the result of '[[ "$drift" == "false" ]] && log ...', i.e. non-zero when drift was detected. Any caller that tested the function's return (or a 'set -e' main that relied on it aborting) now sees success on tampered/missing files. The change is only safe if 'fail' independently records the error into a global counter that drives the script's final exit code.
findings.failure_mode: Integrity drift detected but the script (or a wrapper checking $?) exits 0, silently passing a tampered System Zone.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the drift state explicitly ('[[ "$drift" == false ]]' as the last statement, or 'return 1' when drift is true) and keep the informational not-mounted summary before it, or confirm and document that the fail counter alone drives the exit code.

findings.description: In a submodule mount, any manifest path that is absent locally but present under .loa/<path> is counted as informational 'not-mounted' and never fails. The check has no knowledge of which subset the mount was supposed to link, so a deliberately removed symlink to a security-relevant file (a hook, a gate script, a rules file) is indistinguishable from an intentionally unlinked path. This downgrades tamper-by-deletion from 'Missing (fail)' to a count in a log line for every submodule-mounted project.
findings.failure_mode: An operator or agent deletes .claude/hooks/<gate>.sh symlink in a submodule mount; check-loa.sh reports 'not-mounted: 1 path(s)' and 'Integrity verified'.
findings.suggested_fix: Consult the mount-scope definition used by the mount tooling (the set of paths the mount is supposed to link, which tools/check-manifest-paths.sh appears to validate) and only treat paths outside that set as not-mounted; paths inside the set that are absent should remain 'Missing' failures.

findings.description: The default bats path falls back to a specific operator's dotfiles location ('$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats'). On any other host this resolves to 'bats=absent', which silently changes the fingerprint relative to the author's machine for otherwise identical toolchains, undermining the cross-host comparability the fingerprint exists to provide.
findings.failure_mode: Two hosts with identical bats versions produce different fingerprints (one 'absent', one versioned) purely because of the hardcoded personal path; batch rows become non-comparable.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the personal fallback path; rely on PATH lookup plus --bats-bin / LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN, and document the env var in the header.

findings.description: The header promises that a missing tool reads 'tool=absent' and does not fail the run, and python3 is one of the probed tools. But the digest itself is computed with 'python3 -I -c ...' under 'set -euo pipefail', so a host without python3 exits non-zero and never prints a fingerprint, contradicting the documented contract and failing every caller that fills MANIFEST.json / pipeline.json from this value.
findings.failure_mode: fingerprint.sh exits with 'python3: command not found' instead of emitting a fingerprint containing 'python3=absent'; pipeline-run.sh / run-arms.sh abort before any phase.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same portable sha256 helper the rest of the harness uses (sha256sum / shasum fallback) for the digest, or document python3 as a hard requirement and check for it up front with a clear exit 2 message.

findings.description: ms(ts) strips only a fractional-seconds suffix ending in 'Z' and then calls fromdateiso8601, which accepts exactly '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'. If pipeline.json's started/finished carry a numeric offset ('+00:00'), lack the trailing 'Z', or 'started' is an empty string (the row builder itself defaults 'started' to "" but wall_clock_ms is computed from $p.started directly), jq raises a runtime error and the whole jq invocation fails. Under set -e no row is written and no partial row is appended, so the run disappears from runs.jsonl without a diagnostic row.
findings.failure_mode: ablation-row.sh exits with a jq 'date ... does not match format' error; the batch loses the run's row entirely rather than emitting an infrastructure_error row.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the subtraction with a try: 'try (ms($p.finished) - ms($p.started)) catch (sum of phase durations)', and normalise offsets (e.g. sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z")) before fromdateiso8601.
